review_cost.rationale: I'd approve after one small round: nothing structural, and three concrete asks plus nits. Every change is local and low-risk.

findings.issue: Removing a member updates cards and the count immediately (from TeamProvider state) but the Type coverage table stays stale until router.invalidate() refetches getTeamPage from the cookie; team truth is split between the cookie, the provider, and the server snapshot.
findings.suggestion: Compute the coverage table on the client from data.members' types plus the (already fetched) damage relations, or make the remove handler await the invalidation; single source of truth for the team.

findings.issue: The root head() reads `m._notFound`, a private/internal router match field, to title not-found documents.
findings.suggestion: Rely on the public `m.status === 'notFound'` only, or let the notFound component set its own title via a route head.

findings.issue: Card sprite URLs are constructed from a hard-coded pattern instead of the API-provided `sprites.front_default`, which the spec says is null for unshipped sprite sets.
findings.suggestion: Use the API's sprite URL with the pattern only as a fallback, and render a placeholder when it is null.

findings.issue: typeList() is invoked twice inside the same Promise.all in getTeamPage, relying on the memo cache to avoid duplicate work.
findings.suggestion: Call it once and derive both the label list and the details list from the result.

findings.issue: No errorComponent/onCatch anywhere; an upstream API failure surfaces the framework's default error page with no route back into the app.
findings.suggestion: Add a defaultErrorComponent on the router or root route with a retry link.

findings.issue: The search input is synced to the URL via a lastPushed ref plus two effects; correct but fragile if a second effect ever writes search.q.
findings.suggestion: Document the invariant next to the ref, or collapse to one effect keyed on the debounced value.

findings.issue: Cache eviction only prunes expired entries and only when size exceeds 5000, so a burst of unexpired keys can grow the map (bounded in practice by the API's fixed size).
findings.suggestion: Also cap by inserting order (e.g. FIFO beyond a hard limit) or evict the oldest entry regardless of expiry.

findings.issue: A file named config.ts in lib/ contains a single React hook (useMediaBase), which misleads readers looking for configuration.
findings.suggestion: Rename to useMediaBase.ts (or fold it into an existing hooks/components location).

findings.issue: getHomeData ships the entire 1026-species index (plus types and generations) to the client in the dehydrated loader payload; a deliberate but undocumented trade-off.
findings.suggestion: Add a comment recording the payload/latency trade-off and revisit if the dataset grows.

findings.issue: Generated route tree is committed, so feature PRs carry ~60 lines of generated diff noise (visible in CHANGES.diff).
findings.suggestion: Add src/routeTree.gen.ts to .gitignore since the Vite plugin regenerates it on dev/build.

summary: This is a genuinely idiomatic TanStack Start app on the current stable APIs: file-based routing with validateSearch/loaderDeps, server functions using the canonical `.validator()`, notFound() in loaders, a proper root shell, and an srvx production server that matches the framework's own examples. Server/client boundaries are clean and the TTL cache is well engineered, with no serious correctness bugs — only a stale coverage table on team edits, constructed sprite URLs, and a peek at a private router field. I'd merge after one small round of changes.
